newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's July leading indicators.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's July leading indicators.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' reactions to Japan's closely watched diffusion index of leading economic indicators for July, released on Tuesday, which stood at 77.8 on a scale of 100.

Analysts had anticipated that the July leading index would be above the so-called "boom or bust" 50 percent line for a fourth consecutive month. A figure for the index above 50 is taken as suggesting economic expansion in the coming months.
KUNJI OKUE, ECONOMIST AT KLEINWORT BENSON IN TOKYO:
"Both (leading and concident) indices were above 50. We can translate this as that the economy is still recovering."

Okue told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) that industrial production was key both to the diffusion index and to the Bank of Japan's "tankan" quarterly corporate survey. "For example, the coincident index includes six components related to industrial production activities. So whenever industrial production is found to be very well, that means the coincident index would go up. So regarding Tankan, carried by the Bank of Japan, it also includes many components related to industrial production activities, so the key issue is how industrial production is performing."

"At this moment we have two aspects for industrial production -- domestic demand and exports. So far we have seen relatively strong exports towards Asian countries. Although it's become a little bit sluggish at the moment, there is strong, robust demand for products we have. I don't think we have any big problem at this moment on this side."
YASUSHI OKUDA, ECONOMIST AT BZW IN TOKYO:
"Overall, private capital spending is strong and housing investments are doing okay. The missing component is private consumption."

Okuda told RFTV that the O-157 food poisoning epidemic which swept the nation in July and August was likely to have affected consumption and department and chainstore sales coming out later this week and would be interesting to watch out for.
